storyline.governing_thought: Do not launch Parcelbird Now in 2027: at every observed level its stores lose money per order, and the plan breaks the runway rule; grow the software instead

exec_summary.text: Quick commerce sales nearly tripled from 2022 to 2025, but no operator has yet made it pay

sub_points.text: Zipcart lost $1.90 and QuickBasket $3.40 an order in 2025

exec_summary.text: Parcelbird Now would lose money on every order unless it beats the best observed site on every input

sub_points.text: The median site on our software loses $2.67 an order
The plan needs 3.5 orders per rider-hour; the best site gets 3.0

exec_summary.text: The launch does not fit the cash, even on the founders' own numbers

sub_points.text: The plan falls $2.3M short of the 12-month runway rule at month 18
Nine sites at benchmark would lose about $18M a year

exec_summary.text: Growing the software is the better use of the cash and needs no new funding

sub_points.text: Late-stage grocers alone would add a fifth to today's $4.1M ARR
Cash bottoms out near $5.4M, then grows from year three

exec_summary.text: Decline the launch in January, fund the software plan, and reopen only on evidence

sub_points.text: Hire four people now; reopen only when a median site makes money after site costs

next_steps.action: Decide: decline the Parcelbird Now launch and approve the software plan
Hire two engineers and two sales staff
Close the nine late-stage grocers and scope store-based delivery with them
Bring a software-only budget that tests the flat-cost assumption
Report the 14-site benchmark against the reopening triggers each quarter

problem.statement: Should Parcelbird launch Parcelbird Now, its own 15-minute grocery delivery service, in 2027, given $12.0M of cash and a rule of 12 months of runway at all times?
problem.decision_maker: The board (two founders and two investors), approving or rejecting the launch
success_criteria: A path to profitability within the current $12.0M of cash, with no new round
At least 12 months of runway at all times
Positive contribution per order shown on evidence, not only on plan inputs
problem.accuracy: Directional: per-order economics to about $0.50, cash to about $0.5M

one_day_answer.situation: Parcelbird has a software business growing 60% a year at 81% gross margin and $12.0M in the bank; the founders propose becoming a quick-commerce operator
one_day_answer.complication: Every operator and every site in the briefing pack loses money on each order, and the plan needs $9.5M of the $12.0M with no new round likely
one_day_answer.resolution: Decline the 2027 launch, put the cash into the software business, and reopen the operator question only when site economics are proven
